options.text: POST, because query values belong in the request body.
PUT, because submitting a form always replaces a resource.
GET with each input's name omitted.

options.text: <label for="email">Email</label><input id="email" name="email">
<label name="email">Email</label><input id="email">

<input id="email"><label for="address">Email</label>

questions.prompt: Which statement about a required email input is accurate?

options.text: required guarantees the address exists and can receive mail.
required prevents an empty value, while type=email applies syntax checks but does not verify a mailbox.
type=email automatically makes the field required.
The browser submits the form even when native constraint validation fails.

questions.prompt: A button inside a form only reveals optional help and must not submit the form. What should its type be?

options.text: type="reset", because reset buttons do not submit.
type="submit", then cancel submission with CSS.
type="button".
No type, because a button inside a form has no default behavior.

questions.prompt: Which controls normally contribute a name/value pair when a form is submitted?

options.text: Every visible control, whether enabled or not.
Only controls with an id attribute.
Every checked and unchecked checkbox, plus all submit buttons.
Successful controls, including eligible enabled controls with a name; unchecked checkboxes are omitted.

questions.prompt: In a data table, which markup best identifies the first column as row headers?

options.text: <th scope="row">Ada</th>
Ada
<th scope="col">Ada</th>
Ada

questions.prompt: A decorative divider image adds no information. Which alternative text is appropriate?

options.text: Omit the img element's alt attribute so screen readers infer the image.
Use alt="" so assistive technology can ignore the decorative image.
Use the filename as alt text.
Use alt="decorative image" for every decorative image.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of sizes when an img uses width-descriptor candidates such as photo-480.jpg 480w?

options.text: It sets the image's intrinsic pixel dimensions in the file.
It guarantees the browser downloads only the smallest candidate.
It describes the expected rendered slot width at media conditions so the browser can choose a candidate.
It replaces the need for src or srcset.

<caption src="captions.vtt">
<figcaption src="captions.vtt">
<track kind="captions" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en">

options.text: <button type="button">Save draft</button>
Save draft

<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<meta charset="viewport">
<meta name="device-width" content="responsive">

questions.prompt: For a classic external script with defer, when does the browser execute it?

options.text: Immediately, blocking HTML parsing until the file downloads.
Only after the window load event, regardless of document parsing.
After parsing completes, while preserving document order among deferred classic scripts.
Before parsing begins, with execution order determined by download completion.

options.text: alt="Office location map"
name="Office location map"
aria-describedby="Office location map"
title="Office location map"

questions.prompt: What does form.checkValidity() return?

options.text: A boolean indicating whether the form's associated controls satisfy their constraints.
A promise that resolves after the server validates the form.
The submitted FormData object.
A boolean that is true only after a successful network submission.

questions.prompt: A form field appears in the UI but is missing from the request. Which first check is most directly relevant?

options.text: Confirm the field has a unique class name.
Inspect whether it has a name, is enabled, and is a successful control for this submission.
Add an aria-label; that makes the value submit.
Replace its id with a name attribute; IDs are forbidden on form controls.

questions.prompt: What is the best reason to use heading elements in a meaningful hierarchy?

options.text: Heading levels are only visual sizes; accessibility APIs ignore them.
Every page must use exactly one h1 and no other h1 is valid HTML.
Headings expose document structure to users and assistive technology; choose ranks based on section hierarchy, not desired font size.
A heading element automatically creates a navigation link to itself.

options.text: Partner
Partner
Partner
Partner

questions.prompt: How does a browser use source elements inside picture?

options.text: It checks source elements in order and selects a matching supported candidate, falling back to the nested img.
It downloads every source and composites them together.
It uses the final source regardless of media and type attributes.
It treats picture as a replacement for the required img alternative text.

questions.prompt: What does autocomplete="email" communicate on an email form control?

options.text: It validates the address against the user's mailbox provider.
It is an autofill hint describing the expected kind of value.
It makes the field read-only after the first entry.
It sets the field's submitted name to email.

questions.prompt: Which element gives a data table a concise title or description associated with the table?

options.text: <summary> placed inside <table>
<legend> placed inside <table>
<caption> as a child of <table>
<figcaption> as a child of <tbody>

questions.prompt: What is a practical effect of rel="preconnect" on a link to a third-party origin?

options.text: It downloads every resource from that origin before parsing.
It makes the origin same-origin for CORS.
It guarantees that the later request cannot be blocked.
It lets the browser initiate connection setup early; use it selectively because connections consume resources.

questions.prompt: Which choices support a meaningful semantic page structure?

options.text: Use header and footer for the relevant page or section landmarks.
Use main for the document's dominant content, ordinarily only once.
Use nav for a major group of navigation links.
Replace every div with section, even when the group has no thematic heading.

questions.prompt: Which statements about links and URL references are correct?

options.text: A root-relative path such as /help starts at the origin's root path.
Every relative URL is resolved from the site's origin root, regardless of a base element.
A fragment such as #details can target an element id in the current document.
A URL fragment is always sent to the server as part of the HTTP request path.

questions.prompt: Which practices make a form's controls easier to understand and validate?

options.text: Use placeholder text as the only label because it remains visible after entry.
Give each user-facing control a visible, programmatically associated label.
Use name attributes for values that should be submitted.
Use native constraints such as required or min where they fit, and validate on the server too.

questions.prompt: Which statements describe form submission data accurately?

options.text: A disabled form control is normally omitted from the submitted entry list.
A checked checkbox with a name contributes its value; an unchecked checkbox normally does not.
A control's id is used as the submitted key even when it has no name.
A submit button's name/value can be included when that button is the submitter.

questions.prompt: Which are sound choices for an accessible data table?

options.text: Use table markup for any visual grid, including a page layout.
Use th for header cells and td for ordinary data cells.
Use scope on row or column headers when it clarifies their relationship.
Use caption to identify the table's subject when a caption is useful.

questions.prompt: Which image practices are appropriate?

options.text: Omit alt whenever an image is inside a link.
Use the same long alt text for every candidate in a responsive image set, even if the image's meaning changes.
Use alt="" for an image that is purely decorative and adds no information.
Describe an informative image's relevant meaning in its context rather than mechanically copying its filename.

questions.prompt: Which choices improve the accessibility of interactive HTML?

options.text: Prefer native controls because their roles, keyboard behavior, and states are built in.
Use color alone to distinguish required, invalid, or selected states.
Ensure every form field has a programmatically determinable name.
Keep focus visible and provide keyboard access to custom interactions.

questions.prompt: Which statements about ARIA and native HTML semantics are correct?

options.text: Adding role="button" to a div automatically makes it focusable and keyboard-operable.
Native HTML semantics should generally be preferred when an element already expresses the needed role.
ARIA labels always override visible text in every accessibility naming situation.
ARIA can add semantics or state, but it does not automatically implement keyboard interaction.

questions.prompt: Which resource-loading statements are accurate?

options.text: defer on an external classic script avoids blocking parsing while the file downloads.
async guarantees execution order matching the document order of scripts.
Preload should be reserved for resources needed soon, with the correct as value and compatible resource selection.
A preload guarantees that a resource will be used and improves performance in every case.

questions.prompt: Which practices are appropriate for embedded content?

options.text: Assume sandbox="allow-scripts" also grants same-origin access.
Give an iframe a concise title describing the embedded page or tool.
Use the iframe title as a substitute for checking whether the embedded content itself is accessible.
Use iframe sandbox restrictions deliberately and grant only needed capabilities.

questions.prompt: Which browser API practices can help implement and test form behavior?

options.text: Use form.submit() when native constraint validation and submit events must run.
Use new FormData(form) to inspect eligible named form entries.
Use control.validity or checkValidity() to inspect constraint-validation state.
Use form.requestSubmit() when code should request normal submitter behavior and validation.

questions.prompt: When debugging a form that behaves differently from expectations, which checks are useful?

options.text: Inspect the rendered DOM and the actual network request's method, URL, and payload.
Assume a successful client-side validity check proves the server accepted the data.
Assume the source file alone always shows the final DOM after scripts and parsing.
Check the browser's reported validity state and whether a control is disabled or lacks a name.
